exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean delivery, Vaginal delivery)
outcome: Neonatal gut microbiome composition (Bacteroidota organisms, Firmicutes organisms, Enterococcus genus)
cohort: Participants were neonates from a high-risk, under-resourced Bronx, NY population, whose fecal samples were collected as part of the Bronx MomBa Health Study.
finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a relative reduction of Bacteroidota and an increase in Firmicutes and Enterococcus organisms in the gut microbiome over the first two years of life.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery led to reduced Bacteroidota and increased Firmicutes and Enterococcus organisms in the gut microbiome compared to vaginal delivery.
